bull_case: Buyers gain selection, convenience and financing; merchants gain demand, logistics, payments, ads and credit. Cross-ecosystem usage materially deepens engagement and wallet share.
bear_case: Free shipping and credit can transfer economics to customers faster than MELI earns them back. Strong usage alone does not guarantee attractive unit economics in every product.
thesis: Customer value is very strong. Post-threshold cohorts show higher retention, items and category breadth, while ecosystemic users generate substantially more GMV than marketplace-only users. The main weakness is unit economics: Q2 margin remains compressed and credit-card NIMAL is negative. Demand is not subsidy-only, but the current engagement investments still need full cash-payback proof.

evidence.claim: After Brazil's free-shipping threshold change, new buyer cohorts purchased more items across more categories with higher retention than prior cohorts.
Ecosystemic users generated 70% more GMV and 55% more items per user than marketplace-only users in Q2 2026.
Items per buyer rose 14% YoY and the share of users buying three or more categories reached an all-time high.
Q2 operating margin was 6.7% and credit-card NIMAL was -2.5%, showing that some engagement investments have not yet reached attractive steady-state economics.

counterevidence: Free shipping is an explicit economic subsidy and can mask weak payback if cohort gains fade.
Credit-card economics remain below breakeven on NIMAL.
Merchants and consumers can multi-home across competing platforms.
Adjusted FCF remains compressed despite strong engagement.
unknowns: Credit-card lifetime value after losses and funding costs.
Merchant multi-homing rates and incremental ad ROI.
falsifiers: Post-threshold cohort retention converges back to pre-change levels.
Credit-card NIMAL remains negative without offsetting ecosystem economics.
Usage growth persists while adjusted FCF/share fails to recover for multiple years.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Higher retention, multi-category usage and cross-ecosystem wallet share show recurring customer utility beyond the free-shipping subsidy itself.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: MELI spans commerce, payments, credit, logistics and ads across multiple countries; no single customer or single product is existential.

key_kpis.name: Ecosystemic user wallet share
key_kpis.threshold: retain material GMV/items uplift versus single-vertical users

subscores.rationale: MELI solves multiple regional frictions and post-investment cohorts show durable behavior change, consistent with very strong willingness to use and pay.
Retention, items per buyer, category breadth and cross-ecosystem wallet share are all improving at large scale.
Scale benefits are visible, but current margin compression, low adjusted FCF and negative credit-card NIMAL prevent a 75+ unit-economics score.

uncertainties.rationale: Behavioral evidence is strong even though direct monetary ROI differs by user type.
Multiple cohort and engagement measures support improvement.
Current engagement growth is not yet matched by normalized owner-cash-flow conversion.
